classes.name: Landtagswahlen
classes.finest_note: Counted by municipality; the Oberland and Unterland districts are the contests. Postal and in-person votes are split in the protocol, not by station.
classes.note: 25 members since 1989 (15 for the Oberland, 10 for the Unterland) and 15 before, elected by list PR in the two districts with a national 8% threshold; each voter has as many votes as the district has seats, unused ones count for the list as Zusatzstimmen (Verfassung Art. 46; VRG Art. 55-56). Each list also elects deputy members (stellvertretende Abgeordnete). Majority vote until PR was introduced in 1939; women vote since 1984.

cadence.locator: https://www.gesetze.li/konso/1921015000 (Art. 47 Abs. 1 as amended by LGBl. 1958 Nr. 1; Art. 48 lets the Prince dissolve the Landtag)

https://www.gesetze.li/konso/1921015000 (Art. 47 Abs. 1: four-year term, regular elections in February or March of the year the fourth year ends; Art. 48 and 50: dissolution and a new election within six weeks)
cadence.vacancy_rule: The next unelected candidate of the same list takes the seat; a by-election (Ergänzungswahl) only when the list is exhausted (Verfassung Art. 53)

classes.name: Landtagswahlen nach der Konstitutionellen Verfassung von 1862
classes.name_en: Landtag elections under the 1862 constitution (indirect, through electors)
classes.note: Under the constitution of 26 September 1862, which the 1921 constitution replaced, voters in each municipality chose electors (Wahlmänner) who elected 12 of the Landtag's 15 members; the Prince appointed the other three.
classes.disposition_reason: No official publisher of the returns answers online: the government's results sites begin in 2001, the Landesarchiv's e-archiv.li offers document editions without result tables, and the statistics portal (statistikportal.li) and the national administration's site (llv.li) refuse automated requests.

dates.note: Indirect Landtag elections from 1862 to 1914; not yet counted.

classes.name: Volksabstimmungen
classes.note: The votes of March 1919 and March 1921 came before the constitution, on the government's order. Optional referendums on laws, spending decisions and treaties (1,000 or 1,500 signatures or three or four municipalities), initiatives for laws and constitutional amendments, votes ordered by the Landtag, votes on dissolving the Landtag (Art. 48 Abs. 3), on a motion of no confidence in the Prince (Art. 13ter), and on abolishing the monarchy in two rounds (Art. 113). A counter-proposal or rival initiative is a separate ballot question. The Prince's sanction is still needed for a law passed by the people (Art. 65).

access.evidence: Results pages 1-35 for every national vote from March 2002 to December 2024, by municipality, district, and country, with the voting protocol; pages above 35 are empty.

The Liechtensteiner Volksblatt, the official publication organ, and the other papers of the country print each national vote's result by municipality, from the late 1940s as the government's own notice; the scans carry ALTO text.

classes.name: Volksabstimmung über Richterkandidaten
classes.name_en: Popular vote on a judicial candidate
classes.note: Judges are chosen by a panel the Prince chairs, elected by the Landtag, and appointed by the Prince. Only if the Landtag rejects the panel's candidate and no agreement follows within four weeks do voters choose between the panel's candidate, the Landtag's, and any nominated by initiative, in two rounds when there are more than two (Art. 96 Abs. 2, since the 2003 revision). No such vote has been held.

classes.name: Landesfürst
classes.disposition_reason: The office is hereditary in the princely house under its house law (Art. 3); no one votes on it. A motion of no confidence in the Prince goes to a national vote, which the volksabstimmung class holds.

classes.name: Bestellung der Regierung
classes.disposition_reason: The Prince appoints the head of government and four ministers in agreement with the Landtag on its proposal (Art. 79 Abs. 2); there is no ballot by voters, and the 25 February 2024 initiative to involve the people in choosing the government was rejected.

classes.name: Wahlen im Landtag
classes.disposition_reason: The Landtag's elections of its president and vice-president, the Landesausschuss, and judges are votes of 25 members in session, recorded in the Landtag's minutes, not elections by voters.

classes.name: Unterschriftensammlungen für Initiativen und Referenden
classes.name_en: Signature collections for initiatives and referendums
classes.locator: https://www.gesetze.li/konso/1973050000 (Art. 67-71: Gemeinde- and Sammelbegehren, signature checks and publication)
classes.disposition_reason: Voters sign in support and there is no choice between options, so a signature count is not an election result; abstimmungen.li lists the counts beside each vote. The archive keeps the votes that a successful collection triggers.

classes.name: Nominierung der Kandidaten
classes.locator: https://www.gesetze.li/konso/1973050000 (Art. 37: a nomination needs 30 voters' signatures in the district)
classes.disposition_reason: No nominating contest is run by the state: voter groups file lists with voters' signatures (VRG Art. 37; GemG Art. 73), and the parties choose their candidates at their own meetings.

classes.name: Gemeinderatswahlen
classes.finest_note: Each of the 11 municipalities is one contest.
classes.note: Councils of 6 to 12 members besides the Vorsteher, set by each municipality's ordinance by population (GemG Art. 38), elected by list PR with candidate and additional votes and no threshold (GemG Art. 78-80). The 2003-2011 sites count 117 council seats with the 11 Vorsteher, 2015-2023 115.

cadence.vacancy_rule: The next unelected candidate of the same list takes the seat; a by-election only when the list is exhausted (GemG Art. 46)

classes.name: Gemeindevorsteherwahlen
classes.finest_note: Each of the 11 municipalities is one contest.
classes.note: The Vorsteher heads the council and the municipality; elected by absolute majority, with a second round among the same candidates within four weeks decided by plurality (GemG Art. 71). The Vaduz Vorsteher is styled Bürgermeister.

cadence.runoff_rule: Absolute majority of valid votes; otherwise a new round within four weeks among the same candidates, decided by plurality (GemG Art. 71 Abs. 2-3).
cadence.administered_by: The municipal electoral commissions, on the date the government sets

access.evidence: Council seats by party, the elected Vorsteher, candidates, and turnout per municipality for 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, and 2023 (resultate/3, 2, 1, 9, 11, 14).

dates.note: Vorsteher elections before 2003; not yet counted.
The Schellenberg Vorsteher led with 46.4% in the first round, so a second round followed; second rounds are not on the site and are not yet counted.

classes.name: Wahl der Geschäftsprüfungskommission
classes.note: Each municipality's voters elect a three-member audit committee by ballot within six months of the council election (GemG Art. 35, 56). The government's results sites do not carry these elections; each municipality announces its own.

cadence.locator: https://www.gesetze.li/konso/1996076000 (Art. 56: elected within six months after the council election; three members)

classes.name: Gemeindeabstimmungen
classes.note: Ballot votes (Urnenabstimmungen) that a council orders in place of a municipal assembly, on spending, plans, ordinances, a sixth of voters' referendums and initiatives (GemG Art. 35-42), and a municipality's vote to start leaving the state (Verfassung Art. 4 Abs. 2). Each municipality runs and announces its own.

classes.name: Wahl des Vizevorstehers
classes.disposition_reason: The council elects the Vizevorsteher from its own members within four days of taking office (GemG Art. 82); there is no ballot by voters.
